subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
intro: These problems combine scale-drawing reasoning with area scaling, unit conversion, and re-drawing at a new scale. Work in steps: find the actual figure first, then apply the new scale or required conversion.

items.prompt: A floor plan is drawn at the scale $1\text{ cm} : 2\text{ m}$. A rectangular room measures $6\text{ cm}$ by $4\text{ cm}$ on the plan. Find the actual area of the room in $\text{m}^2$.

steps: Convert each side to actual length using $1\text{ cm} : 2\text{ m}$: width $=6\times 2=12\text{ m}$.
Check by area scaling: drawing area $=24\text{ cm}^2$ times the squared scale factor $2^2=4$ gives $24\times 4=96\text{ m}^2$.

items.prompt: A garden is drawn $5\text{ cm}$ by $3\text{ cm}$ on a plan with scale $1\text{ cm} : 4\text{ m}$. Find the actual area in $\text{m}^2$.

steps: Area scales by the square of the scale factor: $4^2=16$.

items.prompt: A triangle is drawn with base $8\text{ cm}$ and height $5\text{ cm}$ at the scale $1\text{ cm} : 3\text{ m}$. Find the actual area of the triangle in $\text{m}^2$.

steps: Actual base $=8\times 3=24\text{ m}$ and actual height $=5\times 3=15\text{ m}$.
Check by area scaling: drawing area $=\frac{1}{2}\times 8\times 5=20\text{ cm}^2$, and $20\times 3^2=20\times 9=180\text{ m}^2$.

items.prompt: A side of a figure is drawn $5\text{ cm}$ long at the scale $1\text{ cm} : 2\text{ m}$. The figure is to be redrawn at the new scale $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$. How long is that side in the new drawing?

steps: Find the actual length first: $5\times 2=10\text{ m}$.
Apply the new scale $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$: drawing length $=\frac{10}{5}=2\text{ cm}$.
The side measures $2\text{ cm}$ in the new drawing.

items.prompt: A rectangle is drawn $12\text{ cm}$ by $9\text{ cm}$ at the scale $1\text{ cm} : 3\text{ m}$. It is redrawn at the scale $1\text{ cm} : 6\text{ m}$. Give the dimensions of the new drawing.

steps: The new drawing is $6\text{ cm}$ by $4.5\text{ cm}$.

items.prompt: A model bridge is built to the scale factor $\frac{1}{50}$. A support beam on the model is $14\text{ cm}$ long. How long is the actual beam, in meters?

steps: The actual beam is $7\text{ m}$ long.

items.prompt: A map uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 8\text{ km}$. A rectangular national park is drawn $3\text{ cm}$ by $2.5\text{ cm}$. Find the actual area of the park in $\text{km}^2$.

steps: Check: drawing area $=3\times 2.5=7.5\text{ cm}^2$, and $7.5\times 8^2=7.5\times 64=480\text{ km}^2$.

items.prompt: On a blueprint with scale $1\text{ in} : 4\text{ ft}$, a rectangular patio is drawn $6\text{ in}$ by $4.5\text{ in}$. Find the actual area of the patio in square feet.

steps: Check: drawing area $=6\times 4.5=27\text{ in}^2$, and $27\times 4^2=27\times 16=432\text{ ft}^2$.

items.prompt: A drawing at scale $1\text{ cm} : 250\text{ cm}$ shows a wall $8\text{ cm}$ long. A second drawing of the same wall is made at scale $1\text{ cm} : 400\text{ cm}$. How long is the wall in the second drawing? Give the answer as a decimal.

steps: The wall is $5\text{ cm}$ long in the second drawing.

items.prompt: Two cities are $35\text{ km}$ apart in reality. On map A they are $7\text{ cm}$ apart. On map B, drawn at the scale $1\text{ cm} : 10\text{ km}$, how far apart are they, and what is the scale of map A written as $1\text{ cm} : ?\text{ km}$?
items.answer: Map B: $3.5\text{ cm}$; map A scale: $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ km}$

steps: Map A scale: $7\text{ cm}$ represents $35\text{ km}$, so $1\text{ cm}$ represents $\frac{35}{7}=5\text{ km}$.
Map A is drawn at $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ km}$, and the cities are $3.5\text{ cm}$ apart on map B.
solution.answer: Map B: $3.5\text{ cm}$; map A scale: $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ km}$

items.prompt: A square room is drawn $7\text{ cm}$ on each side at the scale $1\text{ cm} : 2\text{ m}$. Carpet costs $\$8$ per square meter. Find the cost to carpet the actual room.
A model airplane is built at the scale factor $\frac{1}{72}$. The real wingspan is $10.8\text{ m}$. Find the model's wingspan in centimeters.

steps: Convert the real wingspan to centimeters: $10.8\text{ m}=10.8\times 100=1080\text{ cm}$.
Apply the scale factor: model wingspan $=1080\times \frac{1}{72}=\frac{1080}{72}=15\text{ cm}$.

items.prompt: A rectangular field is drawn $4\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$ at the scale $1\text{ cm} : 25\text{ m}$. Express the actual area in hectares ($1\text{ hectare}=10000\text{ m}^2$).

A triangular plot is drawn with base $10\text{ cm}$ and height $6\text{ cm}$ at scale $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$. The same plot is then redrawn at scale $1\text{ cm} : 15\text{ m}$. Find the base and height in the new drawing.

steps: Actual base $=10\times 5=50\text{ m}$ and actual height $=6\times 5=30\text{ m}$.
The new drawing has base $\frac{10}{3}\text{ cm}$ (about $3.33\text{ cm}$) and height $2\text{ cm}$.

items.prompt: Drawing X uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 4\text{ m}$ and shows a wall as $9\text{ cm}$. Drawing Y of the same wall uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 12\text{ m}$. How many times longer is the wall in drawing X than in drawing Y?

steps: The wall in drawing X is $3$ times as long as in drawing Y.
